endings.label: Unremembered
endings.description:
"Strange things always happen on the battlefield, and some of them I still haven't figured out to this day. The one that left the deepest impression on me occurred in the winter of 1941. That year, the cold was terrifying, and the snow fell heavily. On the days when the snow was at its heaviest, I suddenly received an order saying that a special friendly force was moving in our direction, and we needed to prepare quarters for them and be ready to receive them. A few days passed, and the snow still hadn't stopped. I received another order saying that that friendly force was calling for help and that we needed to lead our troops to reinforce them. But in that weather, there was no way we could reach them, so our superiors agreed to let us wait until the snow stopped before setting out. Two days later, the snow stopped, but we never received any further word from that unit. After the war, I inquired about this and learned that there were several units that had disappeared just as mysteriously, but no one could say where they had gone. That's war—no one can tell where they will die, or whether anyone will remember them."

—— Interview with a Soviet officer, 1969.
